It turns out you have a fantastic memory, because that theory is remarkably close to actual evolutionary psychology and biology research. While it sounds like one of those things someone made up on the internet, there is legitimate science behind these exact ideas.

Here is how those physical traits map to evolutionary survival and mate selection.

1. The Butt & The Brain: The Gluteofemoral Fat Theory

The theory that fat stored in a woman's hips, thighs, and buttocks directly builds a baby's brain is true.

Human brains are massive relative to our bodies and are incredibly resource-intensive to build. To construct a newborn's nervous system, the body requires a massive supply of DHA (docosahexaenoic acid), a long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid.

  • The Privileged Store: Humans are uniquely fat primates, and women are biologically hardwired by estrogen to store subcutaneous fat in the gluteofemoral (hip and thigh) region. Research (such as studies by evolutionary epidemiologist Will Lassek) shows that this specific lower-body fat is highly enriched with DHA.
  • The Brain Drain: During late pregnancy and especially while breastfeeding, the mother's body selectively melts away this lower-body fat to deliver those specialized fatty acids straight to the baby’s rapidly growing brain.
  • The Evolutionary Cue: Under this theory, a low waist-to-hip ratio (the classic hourglass figure) acts as a visual "honest signal" to a male's primitive brain that a female has abundant, high-quality neurodevelopmental resources reserved to sustain an intelligent offspring.

2. Breasts: The Energy & "Frontal Signaling" Hypothesis

The connection between breasts and milk production is a bit of a trick. In almost all other mammals, females only have enlarged breasts when they are actively lactating. Human females are entirely unique because they develop permanent breasts made of fatty tissue at puberty, long before they ever get pregnant.

Because of this, evolutionary biologists view human breasts less as a milk-delivery tool and more as a reproductive signal:

  • Energy Reserves: Breasts are primarily composed of adipose (fat) tissue, not milk glands. Large fat reserves signal that a woman can successfully survive a famine while nursing a child.
  • The "Butt Mimicry" Theory: Prominent anthropologists like Desmond Morris proposed that as early humans evolved to walk upright and transitioned to face-to-face communication (and copulation), the primary sexual signaling shifted from the rear to the front. The theory suggests that permanent breasts evolved as a frontal mimicry of the buttocks to maintain sexual attraction from a forward-facing view.

3. The Face: The "Wikipedia" of Biological Health

The description of the face as a "Wikipedia" of health is an excellent analogy. In evolutionary biology, facial features—especially symmetry—are heavily vetted biomarkers.

          [ HIGH FACIAL SYMMETRY ]
                     │
      ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
      ▼                             ▼
[ Genetic Quality ]        [ Developmental Stability ]
• Low mutation load        • Resistance to pathogens
• Strong immune system     • Ability to withstand environmental stress
  • Developmental Stability: Growing a perfectly symmetrical face is incredibly difficult. From conception through puberty, a body faces constant stressors: parasites, bacterial infections, poor nutrition, and genetic mutations.
  • The "Good Genes" Signal: A highly symmetrical face serves as a visual proof that an individual's genome is robust enough to withstand those stressors without "buckling." It signals a strong immune system and developmental stability.
  • Hormonal Markers: Features like a defined jawline or high cheekbones also indicate an optimal balance of estrogen or testosterone, which directly correlates with youth and peak reproductive years.

Nature is indeed entirely ruthless. What modern humans experience as a subjective feeling of "attractiveness" or "having a type" is often just our ancient, hardwired neurology scanning a potential partner for data points on immune strength, caloric reserves, and the chemical building blocks required to spin up the next generation.

The realization that human attraction is anchored in things completely outside a person's control—like the "genetic lottery" and the "ZIP code lottery"—can feel deeply discouraging because it highlights just how uneven the playing field is from day one.

When looking strictly at the evolutionary framework, nature doesn’t operate on a principle of fairness; it operates entirely on raw, unyielding utility.

The Compounding Dividends of the "Lotteries"

The stark contrast in how people are perceived and treated is driven by two powerful forces that compound over time.

1. The Genetic Lottery & The Halo Effect

Because primitive neurology interprets physical symmetry and specific fat distributions as markers of high health, modern society unconsciously rewards these traits through a cognitive bias known as the Halo Effect.

  • The Bias: When an individual is physically attractive, people automatically and subconsciously ascribe positive internal traits to them—assuming they are more intelligent, trustworthy, kind, and capable.
  • The Social Dividend: This bias creates an immediate, unearned advantage in job interviews, social interactions, and even the legal system, where attractive defendants statistically receive lighter sentences.

2. The ZIP Code Lottery & Resource Amplification

Genetics provide the raw blueprint, but environment dictates how perfectly that blueprint can be executed. This is where socioeconomic status creates massive divergence:

  • Developmental Stability: Growing up in a high-income area means consistent access to high-quality nutrition, lower exposure to environmental toxins, and superior healthcare. This directly mitigates the environmental stressors that throw off facial symmetry and physical development during youth.
  • The Modern "Grooming Gap": In the modern world, "beauty" is heavily financialized. Things like cosmetic dentistry, advanced skincare, tailored fitness coaching, high-end tailoring, and minor dermatology can elevate a person's baseline appearance by orders of magnitude. Wealth buys the ability to maximize the genetic blueprint to its absolute limit.

The Rebalancing Forces

While the biological and socioeconomic starting lines are undeniably rigged, human social dynamics do introduce a few massive variables that disrupt this strict evolutionary hierarchy. Nature is ruthless, but human culture is complex.

The Shift to "Good Provider" and Personality Markers

In long-term mate selection, physical biomarkers lose their absolute monopoly. Evolutionary psychology shows that for long-term pair-bonding, humans look for completely different sets of indicators:

  • Resource Acquisition & Security: Intelligence, ambition, and financial stability frequently override raw physical metrics in long-term viability.
  • Prosocial Traits: Kindness, emotional stability, dependability, and humor are massive survival advantages when raising offspring or navigating a lifetime together. A highly symmetrical face cannot compensate for a volatile or uncooperative partner over a twenty-year horizon.

The "Matching Hypothesis"

In the real world, human mating markets do not result in a few "genetic winners" taking everything while everyone else gets nothing. The Matching Hypothesis in sociology demonstrates that individuals naturally gravitate toward and form highly stable, successful partnerships with people who match their own overall social and physical value.

The differences in scale are massive and unfair, but the evolutionary programming that got us here is only the baseline—it is the opening hand of the game, not the final score.
